design_goal: Let an admin turn an uploaded question set into a trustworthy, assignable knowledge check in minutes using patterns already established by Policies and Modules, and let a learner complete it with an unambiguous pass/fail outcome and a clear path forward on failure.
constraints: JSON upload is the only question-authoring mechanism, no in-UI question builder
Must reuse the existing Training Library tab, Assign Module wizard, and per-user Training Status table rather than inventing new structures
RBAC is unresolved and must not be guessed
Attempt limit (3) exists but its terminal behavior is undefined
Stillsuit DS v2 patterns only: wizard, table, modal/drawer, badge, accordion/disclosure list
selected_strategy: Quiz as a Policy-shaped standalone content type, assigned through a reused Assign Module wizard
selected_strategy_rationale: Quiz needs its own Library tab and create wizard like Policy (a single-document, standalone content type), but unlike Policy it needs a per-assignment Assessment step (passing score, retake) which only exists in the Assign Module wizard today. Reusing that wizard structure avoids inventing a third assignment pattern in this product area.

alternative_strategies.name: Auto-reassign / cooldown reset on attempt exhaustion
alternative_strategies.summary: After a learner exhausts 3 attempts, automatically grant a new attempt cycle after a cooldown period without admin action.
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Introduces new scheduling logic not present anywhere else in this feature or its closest precedent (Policies), and risks learners treating failure as something to wait out rather than re-engage with.

tradeoffs: Terminal failed state after 3 attempts gives the learner no self-service path back into compliance; admins must notice and manually reassign
Reusing the full 4-step Assign Module wizard is heavier than Policy's single Assign action, even though Quiz is a single-item content type like Policy
JSON-only authoring remains the feature's biggest unresolved trust risk; this strategy treats validation UX as first-class but does not fully specify it pending content design input
assumptions: Assign Quiz reuses the full Assign Module wizard structure (Assignment Type, Assessment, Assign To, Review) per stakeholder decision
Passing score and retake-on-fail are configurable per assignment, pre-filled from quiz publish-time defaults, per stakeholder decision
Quiz-taking withholds feedback until final scoring with no per-question reveal, per stakeholder decision
open_issues: Which roles can create, publish, or assign a Quiz (RBAC undefined)
Exact validation messaging and error taxonomy for malformed/empty/oversized JSON uploads
Whether a published quiz can be edited/re-versioned and whether that forces a retake for already-completed users
Whether Quiz completion feeds the Risk Scoring Engine the same way module assessments do
Whether a dedicated 'New Quiz Assigned' email exists or the generic assignment template is reused
risks: Terminal failure state creates support load if admins don't proactively monitor 'Failed — Attempts exhausted' status
Assign Quiz's Step 1 (Assignment Type) may feel like a pointless single-option screen since a quiz has no 'individual trainings' split like a Module does
Weak JSON validation UX turns the feature's clearest differentiator (bulk question authoring) into its biggest support burden
next_actions: Confirm the attempt-exhaustion strategy (terminal failed state) with PM before wireframing end-user fail states
Design the JSON upload error-state taxonomy with content design before finalizing the Content step
Build Create Quiz and Assign Quiz wireframes on top of existing Assign Module and Policy Library Figma components rather than from scratch
Flag RBAC and email-template open issues to PM now rather than at handoff
